content: Increased functional HCN/Ih is the most parsimonious single generator of the triad (depolarized RMP, sag, rebound) because one conductance reversing near -30 mV and partly open at rest can produce all three.

content: Sag is the defining biophysical hallmark/fingerprint of Ih carried by HCN channels, so sag is HCN-specific and serves as the experimental arbiter between HCN and non-HCN accounts.
note: Sag treated as exclusive to HCN.

content: Three signs as manifestations of one channel: depolarizing sag on hyperpolarization, inward cation current at rest (depolarized RMP), slow deactivation after a hyperpolarizing input (rebound).
note: Rebound via slow Ih deactivation is asserted; T-type route is the alternative (E26).

content: Data do not license concluding the Ih increase is pathological or that Ih should be blocked; the increase could be compensatory, and a block-Ih strategy is not safe without direct evidence.

note: Reflects the question's instruction not to assume pathology.

content: HCN and T-type currents are classic homeostatic effectors that stabilize networks; documented in neuronal cultures, the preparation class of the Wwox model. Quote: "Homeostatic plasticity stabilizes neuronal networks by adjusting the responsiveness of neurons".
note: Report says Wwox model is a culture-class preparation although E01 is described as slices elsewhere (see note file).

content: The measured Ih increase may be a compensatory response to network hyperexcitability rather than the primary lesion.
note: Also H1 compensatory reading.

content: In GAERS, Ih density and HCN1/HCN3 protein are increased in thalamic ventrobasal neurons yet suppress bursting; "the blockade of Ih relieved the suppressed burst-firing" in pre-epileptic P15-P20 and adult animals.
note: Called direct counterevidence that increased Ih is pathological; report also says a genetic epilepsy model in general (L12).

content: Dendritic Ih block can increase excitability by enhancing temporal summation; HCN's epilepsy role is dual (bidirectional), so blocking Ih risks removing a restraining conductance.
note: No citation given for the dual role claim.

content: Cell-type/age constraint: Ih amplitude increases juvenile to adolescence in pyramidal neurons but decreases in PV+ interneurons; a global HCN blocker may act oppositely on excitatory and inhibitory cells and by age.
note: Wwox data come from an immature preparation per report.

content: Wwox data come from an immature in-vitro model; phenotype characterized only in excitatory pyramidal cells; the right target and desired sign of manipulation may change with age.
note: Developmental stage is not specified in the report.

content: WWOX is a validated regulator of cholesterol/HDL, steroid and fatty-acid metabolism; Wwox-null mice show "marked reductions in serum HDL cholesterol concentrations" and altered ApoA-I/ABCA1 and fatty-acid pathways.
note: Serum, not brain or neuronal membrane.

content: Membrane cholesterol tunes HCN gating: disrupting cholesterol-rich ordered membrane domains potentiated firing in nociceptor DRG neurons and facilitated native HCN opening; cholesterol supplementation inhibited HCN and reduced hyperexcitability in pain models.
note: DRG nociceptors, not cortex.

content: PIP2 independently shifts HCN activation to more depolarized voltages.
note: Heterologous/other systems per L142.

content: H2: WWOX loss lowers membrane cholesterol, disrupts ordered membrane domains and/or alters phosphoinositides, shifting HCN gating and raising functional Ih without a change in channel number.
note: Called WWOX-specific, novel route.

content: Lipid route carries its own rescue arm: cholesterol supplementation (or PIP2 manipulation) should normalize sag and RMP if H2 holds.
note: Route/dose of supplementation not specified.

content: H2 constraints: HCN-lipid data are largely from DRG nociceptors, not cortical pyramidal neurons; brain cholesterol is locally synthesized and compartmentalized; myelination competes for lipid flux and is itself WWOX-impaired.
note: Myelination claim uncited. Whether WWOX lipid changes reach relevant cortical pools is untested (L142).

content: Ordered-membrane-domain size is cell-type-specific, constraining H2.

Scaffold route: filamin A normally internalizes HCN1 and restricts Ih; disrupting the interaction "augments endogenous Ih, and enhances the rebound-response". By analogy, loss of a WWOX-dependent trafficking restraint could raise surface HCN1.
note: WWOX-filamin A link is not shown; analogy via WW-domain scaffold identity.

content: H1: increased functional HCN/Ih (transcriptional/homeostatic up-regulation or increased surface channel number) is the shared generator of the triad.
H3: non-HCN dissociable composite, reduced Kv7/K+ leak sets depolarized RMP and increased firing; de-inactivating T-type Cav3 produces rebound; cannot explain sag so cannot be the whole story.
Kv7/KCNQ/M channels control membrane potential and excitability; Kv7 openers (retigabine, SCR2682) are validated anti-epileptic strategies.
note: SCR2682 named only in passing.

content: A persistent immature NKCC1>KCC2 chloride gradient (fitting WWOX maturation failure) could contribute to depolarization/RMP.
note: No WWOX datum on chloride gradient; flagged as confound for RMP.

content: Bumetanide failed to modify epileptogenesis in a TLE model, and has poor brain penetration; caveat on the chloride arm.
note: Both the failure and the poor-penetration statement are cited at L59 to PMID 20573906 (the abstract reports low brain penetration in rats); the report omits that bumetanide plus phenobarbital counteracted behavioural consequences.

content: Post-inhibitory rebound is the signature of de-inactivating low-threshold T-type Cav3 channels, which contribute to excitability, pacemaking and rebound burst firing; enhancement proposed causal in genetic absence epilepsy.
Rebound is not inherently pathological: "an increased susceptibility to drug-induced SWDs both in CaV3.3(-/-) mice" despite abolished rebound bursts.
note: Report quote partly truncated ("both in" before CaV3.3).

content: Neither reduced K+ leak nor T-type current produces a depolarizing sag, so H3 predicts a pharmacological dissociation (sag unaffected by Kv7 opener plus T-type blocker).

Upstream bridge: Wwox loss increases GSK3beta activity across cortex/hippocampus/cerebellum; "Inhibition of GSK3β by lithium ion significantly abolishes the onset of PTZ-induced seizure in Wwox-/- mice".
note: Report calls it "WOREE knowledge base" statement.

content: GSK3beta forms functional interactions with and regulates neuronal voltage-gated Na+ channels, giving a plausible bridge WWOX loss to GSK3beta hyperactivity to altered channel phosphorylation/trafficking, depolarization and firing.

content: Lithium as an already-available pharmacological lever on the GSK3beta route.
Selective GSK3beta inhibitors CHIR99021 or tideglusib as alternatives to lithium, distinct from poorly brain-penetrant channel blockers.
note: Named without citation.

content: ZD7288 (intracellular) or ivabradine as Ih probe on Wwox-KO neocortical slices.
note: Probe, not therapy proposal.

content: Ivabradine: oral dosing reduced seizures only after P-glycoprotein inhibition by elacridar; limited brain availability of HCN blockers. Anti-seizure proof is in thalamocortical absence epilepsy (GAERS).
note: Elacridar named in passing.

content: Retigabine (Kv7 opener) plus TTA-P2 (T-type blocker) co-applied as the H3 probe.
Ivabradine efficacy in thalamocortical absence epilepsy does not transfer automatically to WOREE's NMDAR/gap-junction-dependent neocortical bursting; HCN blockers are circuit-specific.
HCN blockers are poorly brain-penetrant, limiting translation even if H1/H2 are confirmed.

H1 probe: ZD7288 (or ivabradine) on Wwox-KO neocortical slices reading network bursting, not only sag. Rejection: sag/rebound abolished but bursting unchanged or worse rejects causal/therapeutic reading; failure to abolish sag rejects H1 outright.
note: Intracellular route for ZD7288 noted.

content: H2 probe: measure HCN mRNA/protein and Ih activation curve (V1/2, slope). Proportional HCN protein increase with unchanged V1/2 rejects gating-shift; failure to rescue despite confirmed membrane-cholesterol correction also rejects H2.
note: L150 states reverse inference: elevated HCN with unchanged V1/2 "favors H1".

content: Scaffold sub-route: surface biotinylation of HCN1 plus co-localization with WWOX/scaffold partners; predict raised surface HCN1 with little V1/2 shift; test whether restoring HCN1 internalization normalizes Ih and rebound.

H3 probe: co-apply Kv7 opener plus T-type blocker; H3 rejected as primary if Ih blocker alone normalizes RMP, sag and rebound while the combination fails to abolish sag; if the combination normalizes RMP/rebound and sag persists, a non-HCN contribution coexists with HCN-driven sag.
note: Rejection criterion logic partly circular since sag is HCN-specific by assumption (see note).

content: Foundational quantitative Ih characterization: voltage-clamp Wwox-KO vs WT cortical pyramidal neurons for Ih density, activation V1/2/slope, ZD7288-sensitive component, HCN1/2/4 protein and surface expression.
Arbiter protocol: current-clamp comparison of vehicle, ZD7288, retigabine+TTA-P2 on RMP, sag, rebound with parallel network-bursting readout.
note: Report says one slice experiment separates all hypotheses.

content: Cell-type and developmental resolution: repeat core measures in PV+ interneurons and across developmental stages.
Upstream GSK3beta test: lithium or selective GSK3beta inhibitor to see if the triad and network bursting normalize; unchanged triad means GSK3beta-independent.
Single primary study, immature in-vitro model, qualitative electrophysiology; no Ih I-V curves, no HCN1-4 isoform quantification, no input-resistance control (apparent sag depends on R_in).
Replicate in WWOX-deleted human cortical organoids/iPSC neurons at defined developmental stages (priority).

Direct WWOX-to-channel link is inferential: no study has measured HCN/Cav3/Kv7 expression, gating or membrane lipids in WWOX-deficient cortical neurons; GSK3beta-to-channel link in Wwox cortex hypothesized, not demonstrated.
Cross-system extrapolation: HCN-lipid and PIP2 evidence from DRG nociceptors or heterologous systems; relevance to cortical membrane pools untested.
Directionality unresolved: increased Ih and rebound restraining in multiple models; block-Ih must not be a therapeutic premise without network-level evidence.
note: multiple models is supported in the text by one (GAERS) plus CaV3.3 KO.

content: Refuted-as-assumption list: "block Ih" premise; rebound (T-type) causal for seizures; HCN blocker straightforwardly helps WOREE.
Report calls WWOX lipid-gating route "credible, novel, channel-number-independent" and scaffold route a second channel-number route.
